question: For $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix},$$ verify that $B$ is the inverse of $A$.
explanation:
Product $AB$
$$AB=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}=I$$
Product $BA$
$$BA=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}=I$$
Invertibility condition
Since $AB=BA=I$, $B$ is the inverse of $A$. Hence, $$B=A^{-1}$$

options.A: $AB=I$ but $BA\ne I$, so $B$ is not the inverse of $A$.
